About Faire
Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline.

At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores.

With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.
We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

We're looking for a Staff Product Manager to treat Faire's data and ML platforms as products: define clear user needs, measurable outcomes, and a roadmap that accelerates every team building on these foundations. You will make data trustworthy by default and make ML capabilities easy to adopt and operate in production. When the data Faire runs on is high-quality and easy to use, every team that depends on it makes better decisions and ships better products.
ML powers Faire's marketplace, from search and recommendations to personalization. Shared data sits underneath nearly every product decision we make, and AI data agents are how that insight shows up in the day-to-day of building product.

This role sits at that foundation: you will run structured discovery with the engineers, scientists, and product teams who build on these platforms, prioritize the investments that unblock them, and hold the bar on quality, reliability, and adoption.

You will also establish the product-platform operating model — roadmap, intake, adoption, measurement — that Faire can extend as the broader product platform function scales.

Own the path from ML idea to production: run structured discovery with ML engineers and data scientists, prioritize platform investments across training, deployment, observability, and model registry, and drive adoption so usage signals shape engineering priorities.
Measure ML platform success through user outcomes, including time saved, models shipped, and support load, rather than process metrics alone.
Scale the use of AI data agents: own the vision for agentic data insights Product, Design, and Engineering use to shape strategy; prioritize the data-engineering investments agents depend on; drive adoption across product development; and measure success through decisions accelerated and time saved on insight work, not demo metrics.
Increase trust in Faire's core data by defining SLAs, driving pipeline health on datasets the business depends on, establishing data contracts and clear dataset ownership, and making the cross-functional case for quality investments that compete with feature work.
Improve metadata quality, lineage, and discovery so teams can find, trust, and trace data, and establish access controls and durable compliance processes for data deletion, access management, and auditability.
Build the data products internal users actually need through embedded discovery: fact and dimension tables, semantic layers, reusable data products, and first-class discoverability and developer experience.
Establish a durable product-platform operating model with a published roadmap the company can plan against, a clear intake process, adoption tracking across usage, retention, and satisfaction, and platform cost and efficiency as a health metric — proven first on data and ML, and built to extend as Faire's product platform function grows.

8+ years of product management experience, with ownership of complex technical products at Staff or Lead scope.
Technical fluency across data and ML platforms: you have worked directly with data and ML systems, can engage credibly with engineering on architecture tradeoffs, understand modern ML in production (model training and deployment, feature pipelines, evaluation), and translate technical complexity into clear strategic choices.
Experience shipping platform products for internal technical users, including discovery, success metrics, adoption, and operational discipline.
Experience shipping in a marketplace or other data-rich product context where the product depends on data feeding algorithmic choices such as search, recommendations, or personalization. You understand how upstream data and ML decisions translate into conversion, relevance, and retention.
Cross-functional influence and strategic prioritization: credibility with senior engineers and data scientists, the ability to negotiate without positional authority, ruthless sequencing, and clarity about what the team is choosing not to do.
Comfort building an operating model, not just a roadmap: you have established discovery, intake, and measurement practices that other teams could adopt, and you are energized by growing a platform practice beyond its initial domain.

Established in 2020, Riot Singapore is a game development studio focused on delivering great experiences to our players. We partner with our Los Angeles headquarters on game development for League of Legends, Teamfight Tactics, VALORANT, and unpublished R&D products. Riot Singapore is seeking talented, passionate Rioters with backgrounds in all areas of game development to build games that make it better to be a player.
That’s where you come in.
Game Product Managers at Riot lead passionate teams to create and evolve products and experiences for our players. We seek to deeply understand our product’s audience and drive strategy to create value for players and for Riot. We help concept, build, and influence projects at all stages of production.
As Principal Game Product Manager, Cosmetics for Teamfight Tactics (TFT) , you will lead the TFT Cosmetics team within the Acquisitions, Expression, and Events (AXE) initiative. You will own the vision, strategy, roadmap, and product outcomes for TFT's cosmetics portfolio, spanning existing offerings, new content types, exclusive content, store features, and long term cosmetics research and development.
This is an individual contributor role in which you will serve as the product lead for a multidisciplinary team in Singapore, setting product direction, defining priorities, and driving product decisions across producers, artists, designers, analysts, researchers, marketing partners, and other specialists.

While you will not have formal people management responsibilities, you will be expected to lead through influence, bringing teams together around a shared strategy and empowering them to deliver exceptional player experiences.
Working closely with TFT leadership and stakeholders in our Los Angeles headquarters, you will balance player insights, creative ambition, and commercial outcomes to shape the future of TFT's cosmetics portfolio. Success in this role means creating cosmetics that resonate with players, building a healthy and innovative portfolio, and establishing a long term strategy that supports TFT's continued growth.

Define the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for TFT's cosmetics portfolio, driving player engagement and commercial success.
Lead the multidisciplinary cosmetics team by defining product priorities and aligning partners around them.
Collaborate with artists to create content that resonates deeply with players, elevating their creative vision to achieve product goals.
Manage product KPIs, leveraging performance reporting, experimentation, revenue models, and deep dive analysis and research to improve decision making.
Identify product challenges and opportunities, including cosmetics research and development, formulate strategies and plans, and build stakeholder buy in.
Develop decision frameworks, product briefs, and other artefacts that guide downstream decisions and create clarity across teams.
Partner with Production to translate strategy into executable plans, including roadmap sequencing, capacity planning, prioritization, and sustainable live operations.
Navigate the broader TFT and Riot organization to drive cohesive action across Marketing, Regional Publishing, IP and League Creative, Brand Partnerships, and other cross functional partners.

8+ years of Product Management experience in the games industry, with a strong focus on live-service games where cosmetics and virtual goods are core to the product.
Proven experience owning product vision, strategy, roadmaps, and commercial outcomes while leading cross-functional teams through influence.
Deep expertise in cosmetics, live-service monetization, and player-facing content, with experience shaping product portfolios and driving long-term strategy.
Deep understanding of cosmetics-driven free-to-play games and the player motivations, progression systems, and live-service mechanics that drive long-term engagement.
Proven ability to shape product decisions through player insights, data, commercial thinking, and creative judgement.
Experience partnering with artists, designers, creative directors, and Production to translate creative vision into successful product strategy.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Strong analytical skills, using product performance, player behaviour, experimentation, and market trends to drive strategic decisions.

Experience working in Agile production environments.
Experience working in a cross-geographical, multi-team environment.
Active Teamfight Tactics player with a deep understanding of the game's systems, player base, and cosmetics ecosystem.

Join Truecaller – The place where innovation meets impact!
Truecaller's mission is to build trust in communication by making it safer, smarter, and more efficient. Born in Sweden, trusted by the world, and here’s why we stand out:
We are trusted by over 500 million active users every month across 190+ countries
We identify over 15 billion calls daily, helping users avoid spam and scams
We are powered by a team of 400+ employees from 45+ nationalities
We always look for people who take initiative, own their work, and keep raising the bar. An entrepreneurial mindset matters here, especially when it turns bold ideas into real actions. Truecaller's ads business reaches over 400 million users and is one of the largest in-app advertising platforms in its markets.

We are building a modern, server-driven programmatic stack that we own end to end, and this role owns the platform at the heart of it: the intelligence layer that powers demand-supply matching across all our demand channels.

Every ad opportunity flows through this platform, and it decides how that opportunity is valued, priced, auctioned, and allocated to maximize revenue while protecting user experience.
This is a senior, high-ownership role at the center of a multi-year platform build, working closely with engineering, data science, and the supply and demand product teams.

Own the platform strategy and roadmap: the decisioning, auction, and pricing systems that sit between our supply and our demand partners.
Build auction intelligence: bid landscape analysis, pricing and floor strategies, auction design, and demand orchestration that decides which demand sources to invoke for each opportunity.
Drive yield: deliver measurable improvements in eCPM, fill, win rate, and incremental revenue; identify revenue leakage and close it through platform enhancements.
Optimize for scale: drive initiatives around platform performance, reliability, and latency as traffic volumes and demand partners grow.
Shape the long-term architecture: capabilities like traffic shaping, audience-based packaging, and curated marketplaces that turn the platform into a durable competitive advantage.
Run a rigorous operating cadence: define platform KPIs and operational health metrics, design controlled experiments, and iterate based on measured impact.

6+ years in product management, with 3+ years in ad tech, programmatic advertising, or publisher monetization platforms. Hands-on experience driving revenue growth through programmatic is essential.
Programmatic depth: Strong understanding of the ecosystem, including unified auctions, header bidding, open bidding, mediation models, oRTB, and auction dynamics. Working knowledge of platforms such as Google Ad Manager, PubMatic, or ironSource.
Monetization fluency: comfort with the full KPI stack (eCPM, fill rate, match rate, win rate, bid density, viewability, ARPU) and a track record of using it to find and capture yield.
Platform product skills: proven experience building large-scale platform products with engineering-heavy teams, and the ability to translate complex business problems into scalable platform capabilities. Good understanding of distributed systems, APIs, and latency-sensitive architecture.
Data-driven rigor: strong analytical skills, comfort with large datasets, and fluency in experimentation, A/B testing, and controlled rollouts.
Stakeholder influence: ability to align engineering, data science, ad operations, and sales around a common platform strategy using data and business insight.

This position is needed to build extraordinary tools and solutions for our rapidly growing Global Partnerships team in conjunction with our Go-To-Market (GTM) teams. We are the drivers of the system, process, and data improvements that unlock new possibilities across our Sales, Channel Marketing, and Strategy organizations.
This Product Owner, PRM will work to design, manage, and build scalable solutions, specifically for how we manage, enable, and co-sell with our global partner ecosystem.

This is a great role for an experienced Product Owner who is looking to partner with our global stakeholders, leadership, and builders to execute a roadmap that operationalizes highly-visible channel goals alongside critical Keep the Lights On (KTLO) work.

This includes optimizing our Impartner platform, ensuring seamless integration with Salesforce, and maximizing partner portal engagement.

Bridge Business & Tech: Serve as the strategic liaison between the Partner teams and technical teams, ensuring all business requirements are fully documented, articulate the “what” and “why,” and are clearly understood by platform developers.
Map & Optimize Processes: Analyze and document "as-is" and "to-be" process flows to identify gaps, friction points for partners, and automation opportunities that can be converted into technical requirements.

Drive End-to-End Delivery: Collaborate with end-users, technical squads, and change enablement teams from initial discovery through requirements gathering, build, user acceptance testing (UAT), and deployment.
Own the PRM Roadmap: Maintain a quarterly operational roadmap of enhancements for the partner experience, targeting increased channel efficiency, accurate pipeline reporting, and readiness for scale.
Measure What Matters: Set and track critical metrics for all initiatives. You know that a project doesn't end when a feature drops into production, but rather when partner adoption spikes and measurable operational targets are hit.

Ruby Labs is a leading tech company that creates and operates innovative consumer products. We offer a diverse range of opportunities across the health, education, and entertainment industries. Our innovative teams are driving the future of consumer-led products, and we're always looking for passionate individuals to join us. Learn more about our story at: https://rubylabs.com/about-us/

We are looking for a highly organized Project Owner to own execution quality across one of our D2C subscription products. You will be fully responsible for keeping every workstream moving to standard - setting priorities with stakeholders, translating them into clear technical tasks, driving delivery across product, engineering, design, data, and marketing, and taking direct ownership of projects that have no dedicated owner.
This is a high-accountability role suited for someone who treats "almost done" as not done. We hold a high bar: clear tickets, honest timelines, and work shipped to standard. You will inspect the work, keep the team moving when pace or quality slips, and close gaps yourself when a project falls between roles.

Execution Ownership & Process
Set priorities together with stakeholders and maintain a single, agreed backlog
Own the delivery pipeline end to end, from prioritized backlog to verified release
Define and enforce processes, definitions of done, and quality standards across all workstreams
Drive sprint planning, task tracking, and follow-through so nothing stalls silently
Identify process bottlenecks and fix them with structure, not workarounds
Task Definition & Technical Clarity
Translate product and business priorities into precise, developer-ready technical tasks
Write specs with clear acceptance criteria, edge cases, and measurable outcomes
Partner with engineering to scope, estimate, and sequence work realistically
Use AI tools daily to accelerate spec writing, analysis, and QA - and spread what works across the team
Verify delivered work against spec before it ships — and reject what falls short
Standards & Team Accountability
Hold every contributor to explicit quality and deadline expectations
Push pace and raise the bar when execution drifts, directly and constructively
Run reviews and retros that convert misses into changed processes
Institutionalize best practices so quality does not depend on individual heroics
Cross-functional & Unowned Projects
Take direct ownership of initiatives that lack a dedicated owner and drive them to completion
Coordinate across product, engineering, design, data, and marketing to unblock dependencies
Collaborate with the Managing Director to align execution priorities with business goals
Keep stakeholders informed with concise, honest status reporting

Must-Have Experience
3+ years as a Project Owner, Product Manager, or Delivery/Project Lead on a live software product
Proven track record writing technical tasks and specs that engineers execute without back-and-forth
Experience running agile delivery processes (backlog management, sprints, releases) end to end
Demonstrated ability to build processes, checklists, and quality standards - not just follow them
Experience holding cross-functional contributors accountable for deadlines and quality
Working technical fluency: able to discuss implementation trade-offs with engineers credibly
Advanced, daily use of AI tools (LLMs, agents, AI-assisted workflows) to accelerate specs, analysis, and delivery - with command of standard task-management tooling (Jira, Linear, Notion, or equivalent)
Leadership Attributes
Highly structured operator - you build systems that make quality repeatable
Comfortable giving direct, specific feedback and enforcing standards without drama
Bias to ownership: picks up unclaimed problems instead of waiting for assignment
Detail-obsessed about the work itself - reads the ticket, tests the feature, checks the numbers
Clear, direct communicator who operates effectively in a remote environment
Location
Ruby Labs operates within the CET (Central European Time) zone. Applicants from any country are welcome to apply for the position as long as they are located within approximately ± 4 hours of CET. This ensures optimal collaboration and communication during working hours.

Depth in conducting research and bringing market trends, customer and competitive insights to facilitate strategic ideation to identify opportunities for strategic growth.

About Docker
Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.
We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.
_______________________________________________________________________
AI agents are changing how everyone works — not just developers writing code, but entire organizations building, deploying, and operating software. Agents are becoming teammates: they write code, run tests, manage infrastructure, analyze data, and automate workflows across every function.

Docker is building a new platform from scratch to make this real — secure execution environments, agent-to-tool connectivity, governance controls, and the infrastructure that lets agents and humans collaborate safely at enterprise scale.
This is a 0-to-1 role. You will define the product strategy and own the roadmap for a new platform that sits at the intersection of AI, containers, and developer experience. You will work with a small, high-velocity team spanning engineering, design, and go-to-market to figure out what to build, ship it, learn from it, and iterate. The early signal is already in market — Docker Sandboxes is one of the fastest-growing new products in Docker’s history — and the opportunity ahead is much larger.
We are looking for someone who builds, not just plans. You should be comfortable prototyping, getting your hands dirty with early product iterations, and improvising when things don’t go as expected. The right candidate has shipped developer tools or infrastructure products, understands how the agentic AI ecosystem is evolving, and thrives in the ambiguity of building something genuinely new.

Own the product strategy. Define the vision, roadmap, and success metrics for Docker’s AI & Agent Platform. Make hard tradeoff decisions about what to build, what to defer, and what to cut.
Build from zero. This is a new platform. You will define the product from the ground up — writing the first specs, prototyping with engineering, validating with customers, and iterating rapidly based on what you learn.
Drive from conception through delivery. Write requirements, work with engineering to scope and prioritize, ship iteratively, and measure outcomes. You don’t hand off specs and wait — you are in the details.
Define how pieces of the agentic ecosystem fit together. Agents need secure execution, tool connectivity, model access, governance, and observability. You will define how these capabilities compose into a coherent platform — and where Docker’s boundaries are.
Think beyond developers. Agents are becoming essential for everyone who builds, deploys, and operates software. You will ensure the platform serves the full range of people who need agents to succeed — from individual developers to platform teams to enterprise operators.
Define the developer experience. Work with design and engineering to ensure that our AI products are intuitive, powerful, and meet people where they are — whether in the CLI, IDE, or CI pipeline.
Collaborate across Docker. You will work cross-functionally to ensure coherent product experiences and go-to-market alignment.
Influence technical direction. Partner with engineering leadership on architecture decisions. You don’t need to write the code, but you need to understand the technical tradeoffs and have informed opinions about them.
Represent the customer. Engage directly with developers, enterprises, and partners. Bring their voice into every product decision.
Overcome blockers. When something is in the way — a missing integration, an unclear market signal, a technical constraint — you figure out a path forward. You don’t wait for someone else to solve the problem.

Experience . 10+ years of product management experience, with at least 5 years on developer tools, infrastructure, or platform products.
Deep technical fluency. You can read an architecture diagram, understand container and VM runtimes, and have a working knowledge of how AI agents, LLMs, and protocol-level tool connectivity work. You don’t need to be a hypervisor engineer, but you need to hold your own with one.
Proven ability to ship 0-to-1 products. You have taken a product from idea through launch in a fast-moving environment. You know how to operate when there is no playbook.
Builder mentality. You prototype, you sketch architectures, you test early ideas with customers before the spec is done. You are a doer, not just a thinker.
Strong product sense and UX instincts. You care about the developer experience at a deep level — from API design to CLI ergonomics to error messages.
Strategic thinking with execution follow-through. You can set a multi-year vision and also write the spec for what ships next sprint.
Comfort with ambiguity. This space is new and moving fast. You thrive when the answer isn’t obvious and you have to go find it.
Excellent communication. You can write a crisp product brief, present to executives, and debate technical tradeoffs with engineers — all in the same day.
Experience growing and monetizing products at scale. You have been part of taking a product from early adoption to meaningful revenue, and you understand the pricing, packaging, and go-to-market decisions that make that happen.

Experience building products in the containers, cloud-native, or DevOps space
Experience with AI/ML developer tooling or the agentic AI ecosystem
Contributions to open source projects
Experience building and scaling a business from zero to significant ARR
What You’ll Work With
We are building a new platform for agentic development. Docker Sandboxes — isolated execution environments for AI coding agents — is one of the first products in this platform and one of the fastest-growing new products in Docker’s history. But this is just the beginning. The platform will grow to span multiple product areas as we define how agents and people work together at scale.

We are looking for a Lead Product Manager to own the future of the Lattice MCP (Model Context Protocol) server and the integrations that power Lattice AI.

This is the connective layer that lets customers use Lattice performance data inside the AI tools they already work in (Claude, ChatGPT, Glean, Microsoft Copilot, and Slack), and that brings third-party productivity data (e.g., Jira, GitHub, Linear, Zoom, Asana) into Lattice.

As AI becomes the center of gravity for how companies work, this surface is how Lattice stays connected, interoperable, and indispensable. You’ll join a fully staffed engineering team ready to execute, and together you’ll make ecosystem interoperability a reason customers choose and stay with Lattice.
If you enjoy solving complex problems, shaping platform strategy, and working with great internal and external partners, you’ll love the impact you can have here. As a Lead Product Manager for MCP & AI Ecosystem, you will:
Own the MCP and AI ecosystem strategy. Not only decide what features and integrations to pursue, but what MCP and AI mean to Lattice and our customers. Become a thought leader on how AI should shape HR for the better.
Ship integrations that create leverage. Deliver new MCP tools, resources, and third-party connectors that expand what admins, managers, and executives can do with Lattice data in the flow of work.
Build durable foundations, like authentication, agentic execution frameworks, and evals that make future integrations faster, more scalable, and easier to adopt and maintain.
Be a technical thought partner to Engineering. Help shape technical direction on MCP tool design and third party integration infrastructure, translating complex constraints into clear product decisions.
Drive go-to-market with partners. Partner with Partnerships, Product Marketing, to launch integrations that deliver measurable customer and ecosystem impact.
Own outcomes. Influence and own key results across integration and MCP adoption, reliability, activation, and ecosystem growth.
What You Will Bring to the Table
We’re looking for a seasoned product manager with the technical depth and strategic instincts to shape Lattice’s next generation of integrations and APIs. You’ll be a great fit if you have a combination of:
7+ years of product management experience, with meaningful ownership of integrations, platform, or ecosystem surfaces (built end-to-end, not just configured).
Direct experience building technical integrations in a multi-party ecosystem — for example ad technology / marketing technology, marketplaces, developer platforms, payments, data connectivity, or similar — where partnership strategy shaped what you built.
Strong technical fluency: comfortable with third-party integration patterns, data sync and field mapping, webhooks, and auth/OAuth; you can hold a credible architecture conversation with engineers and partner CTOs.
A track record of shipping scalable, reliable integrations in partnership with engineering, and of standing up partner or marketplace launches with go-to-market teams.
Evidence of turning a platform or ecosystem into a competitive advantage — a reason customers chose your product, not just a checkbox.
Clear, confident communication that brings internal teams and external partners into alignment.
A bias for action and the ability to create structure in an ambiguous, fast-moving space.

Exposure to AI ecosystems, MCP, AI agents, or LLM tooling (helpful, not required).
Experience in multi-product B2B SaaS, or with HR/people-data or other sensitive-data workflows.
If you have strong experience with integrations, APIs, or platform products, even if you don’t meet every preferred qualification, we encourage you to apply. We’re looking for strong product thinkers with deep technical fluency, not perfect resumes.

Webflow is the agentic web marketing platform for modern marketing teams, helping organizations build, manage, and optimize high-performing web experiences that drive predictable growth and strengthen brand trust. Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality.
We're looking for an experienced Product Manager to own how people extend Webflow with code, whether they're developers writing it themselves or the AI agents increasingly writing it alongside them. Our Code team builds the surfaces that bring code-based primitives into Webflow and keep them in sync with the rest of the platform.
This is where Webflow's visual canvas meets real code. It's one of the hardest and most interesting seams in the product, connecting a visual way of building to the code underneath it so that neither one holds the other back. You'll own that seam, deciding how far the two worlds reach into each other and making the connection feel native to developers and agents.

Location: Remote-first (Argentina)
Full-time
Permanent, full-time employee (this is not a contractor position)

Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled
This posting is for a new position
Reporting to the Director of Product Management, Develop
As a Senior Product Manager, Code, you’ll …
Build for developers and AI agents alike. You'll design surfaces that serve the developers who have always worked in code and the AI agents that increasingly write it, treating both as first-class users.
Own the roadmap and delivery across the Code surfaces. You'll lead the products that let developers and agents extend Webflow with code, starting with code components, in close partnership with Engineering, Design, and Data.
Define what "good" means for extensibility. You'll set the quality bar for developer-grade extensibility, including the hard problem of keeping a visual product and real code faithful to each other as each side changes.
Make it all work as one. Several of these surfaces grew up separately. Sequence the work so the pieces reinforce each other and build shared primitives once, rather than solving the same problem twice.
Contribute heavily to strategy, then ship it. You'll help shape where the area goes and turn that into a roadmap you deliver against, working as a partner rather than waiting to be handed direction.
Get into the code. This is a hands-on role. You'll prototype, read and reason about code, and stay close enough to the implementation to make sharp technical calls.
Place durable bets in a shifting landscape. Developer tooling and AI-assisted coding are moving fast, and you'll make choices that hold up as the tools and the ecosystem evolve.

BA/BS degree or equivalent experience
Business-level fluency to read, write and speak in English

Relate to your users and hold more than one perspective at once. You have real empathy for the people you build for and can see a problem through several sets of eyes, balancing needs that pull in different directions without losing sight of any of them.
Enjoy the full craft of building software. You're curious about every part of how products get made and like getting into the details wherever the work needs you, whether that's leading a user interview, prototyping an idea, writing a query to pin down a metric, or writing a sharp brief.

Monetization Instincts: Deep understanding of modern hybrid economies, early subscription funnels, and e-commerce psychology (retention, conversion, instant consumption hooks) that drive high player value.

Execution & Ownership: Hands-on experience as a clear Feature Owner, with a track record of writing clean, analytical PRDs and managing backlogs strictly by commercial impact.

In Deutschland stehen über 3,3 Millionen Mehrparteienhäuser – und sie sind das schwarze Loch der Energiewende. <1% Solardurchdringung. <2% Smart Metering. Kaum Flexibilität oder intelligentes Energiemanagement.
Gleichzeitig zwingt die Regulierung Eigentümer zu massiven Investitionen: Solar wird zur Pflicht, Smart Meter müssen in den nächsten 5 Jahren flächendeckend ausgerollt werden, Heizung und Mobilität elektrifizieren sich. Das Mehrfamilienhaus wird vom Betongold zum aktiven Teil der dezentralen Energieinfrastruktur.
Was fehlt, ist ein integriertes System, das diesen Wandel wirtschaftlich und operativ beherrschbar macht.
VREY kombiniert zertifizierten Messstellenbetrieb mit eigener Software und ermöglicht Eigentümern erstmals, ihren selbst erzeugten Solarstrom direkt an ihre Mieter zu verkaufen – einfach und ohne selbst zum Energieversorger zu werden (§42b EnWG).
Damit wird regulatorischer Zwang zu einer profitablen und planbaren Chance:
Zweistellige Renditen und Wertsteigerung für Eigentümer,
~20 % Stromkostenersparnis für Mieter, und
digitale Infrastruktur für Speicher, Wärmepumpen und Flexibilität.

Im Zuge unserer Seed-Finanzierung haben wir 3,3 Mio. € von führenden Impact- und Energy-VCs (u. a. Rubio Impact Ventures, HTGF, Kopa Ventures) eingesammelt. Mit dem frischen Kapital gehen wir in die nächste Wachstumsphase und bauen unser Team gezielt aus.
Wir stehen am Anfang eines strukturellen Marktumbruchs. Wer heute die Energieinfrastruktur im Mehrfamilienhaus definiert, prägt sie für Jahrzehnte. Werde Teil von VREY und baue mit uns das führende EnergyOS.

s.h: OWN THE CORE PLATFORM STRATEGY & ROADMAP
s.t:
Define and communicate the product strategy and roadmap for the Core Platform in partnership with Engineering and Product leadership.
Prioritize foundational investments based on customer impact, enterprise needs, technical risk, and engineering effort, and make trade-offs between near-term customer needs, technical debt, and long-term architecture explicit.

Drive work on the scalability and reliability of n8n's execution engine, including areas like worker pools and distributed execution.

Establish clear success measures and keep the squad accountable for outcomes, not only delivery.

Nium provides global infrastructure for real-time cross-border payments. We were founded on the mission to deliver the global payments infrastructure of tomorrow, today. Our platform enables banks, fintechs, and global businesses to move money instantly, everywhere.
Co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore with offices in 14 markets worldwide, we are entering one of the most exciting chapters in our journey. In March 2026, we delivered the largest month in our 11-year history with record revenue, record volumes, and EBITDA profitability. Today, Nium moves nearly $60B in payments annually, almost entirely for enterprises, while continuing to strengthen an already healthy balance sheet.
It is an incredible time to join us, and we are only just getting started.
Our payout network spans 190+ countries and 100 currencies, with 100 + corridors in real time. We power seamless transfers to accounts, wallets, and cards, support local collections in 35 markets, and as a principal card issuer on Visa, Mastercard, Discover, and UATP, Nium issues over 50 million card tokens every year.

Backed by regulatory licenses in 40+ markets, we make it simple for our partners to onboard, integrate, and scale globally.

This scale and innovation have earned us recognition as one of CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025, winner of Best Cross-Border Payments Solution at the PayTech Awards, and inclusion in FXC Intelligence’s Top 100 Cross-Border Payments Companies list.
In 2024, we raised US$50 million in Series E funding at a US$1.4 billion valuation to accelerate network expansion, product innovation, and talent growth. With the B2B payments market projected to hit US$175 trillion by 2030, Nium offers ambitious builders the chance to shape the future of global money movement with the scale of a leader and the energy of a high-growth company.

When a contractor in Brazil gets paid on time, a business in Singapore settles in the right currency, or a payroll platform moves money to 40 countries without a single failure: that's what a good payments platform looks like from the outside. From the inside, it's hard decisions about which rails to build on, what reliability means at scale, and how to make a platform handling billions a month behave consistently across markets with completely different rules.
Nium processes cross-border payments for banks, fintechs, and enterprise platforms across 100+ countries. The Senior PM - Payments Platform owns the rails those payments run on.

Reliability. Define what "good" looks like for corridor performance, settlement success, and straight-through processing. Set the targets, own them, move them.

Corridor and market design . Each market has its own mechanics and failure modes. You translate that into requirements: what the corridor supports, how failure is handled, what go-live looks like, so the products built on top can make promises to customers and keep them.

Integration standards. You set the bar for what gets built with correspondent banks, local networks, and processors globally. You decide which integrations are worth doing, weighing partner economics and business impact against build and maintenance cost, and you push the ones that matter through to delivery.

Resilience. Design for failure: redundancy, failover, degraded modes. The goal is a platform where a single rail going down doesn't mean customers feel it.

AI and agentic payment flows . This is the frontier. Payments infrastructure today is reactive: something breaks, someone fixes it. We want infrastructure that thinks: routes intelligently, detects degradation before customers feel it, reconciles autonomously, resolves failures without human escalation. Nium wants to be the first payments infrastructure company to make agentic flows core to how money moves. You define what that looks like and build it.

Payments experience at real scale: high volume, multi-market, genuine accountability when things break. You understand the mechanics (settlement windows, return codes, reconciliation, failure handling) well enough to bring unambiguous requirements.

Curious about how payments work across markets. AI-native in how you work. Rigorous about prioritization. Opinionated, not passive: you form a point of view on how a corridor or integration should work, and you push it forward rather than waiting to be told what to build.

You push Engineering on trade-offs and bring them along with you, holding ground on what's right for the corridor and the business without needing positional authority to do it. And above all, you are passionate about the customer outcome at the end of the transaction, not the platform for its own sake.

3-5 years in product management. Payments, fintech, or financial infrastructure is a requirement. Experience with real-time rails (UPI, SEPA, RTP, Pix, or equivalents) is a strong plus.

The Opportunity

Most payments PMs work on one market, one rail, one product type. Here you work on all of them simultaneously: Asia-Pacific, Americas, Europe, MENA, all with different mechanics and failure modes. The exposure you get in two years compresses what usually takes a decade.

The team is small, senior, and ambitious. The infrastructure you build will process tens of billions of dollars a month and affect the finances of real people and businesses, including the first generation of payments that run through AI agents rather than human-initiated flows.

How We’ll Measure You

Corridor success rate and STP rate, moved quarter over quarter.

Settlement failure rate and time-to-resolution.

Integration delivery against committed dates.

Reduction in payment failures from platform-layer decisions.

Who We Are
At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me , Do the Right Thing , and Get Things Done . These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.
About The Opportunity
OKX is expanding its presence across Latin America, and we're looking for a locally embedded Product Manager to drive market growth in the region. This role sits at the intersection of local market strategy and product execution — you'll identify business and product opportunities unique to LatAm, shape how we localize the trading experience, and own the end-to-end user trading journey for the region.
This is not a "translate and ship" role. We need someone who deeply understands how LatAm users discover, onboard, trade, and grow — and who can turn that understanding into product decisions that move our regional metrics.
What You’ll Be Doing
Local Market Opportunity & Strategy
Identify and prioritize business and product opportunities specific to Latin American markets, including regional payment rails, local trading behaviors, regulatory nuances, and competitive gaps.
Build and maintain a deep understanding of the LatAm crypto and fintech landscape — including key competitors, user segments, regulatory trends, and macro factors that influence trading adoption.
Develop go-to-market product strategies tailored to LatAm user segments (e.g., first-time crypto users, active retail traders, remittance-driven users).
Partner with regional BD, marketing, and operations teams to align product initiatives with local growth objectives.
User Trading Journey Ownership
Own and optimize the full user trading journey across APP and WEB — from discovery and onboarding (Markets, Chart analysis) through execution (Order placement, Chart trading, Position management) to post-trade review (Asset analysis, Trading journal).
Define and execute the product roadmap for trading experience improvements in the region, balancing global platform capabilities with local user needs.
Analyze user behavior, funnel data, and feedback specific to LatAm markets to identify pain points and high-impact opportunities for conversion, retention, and engagement.
Develop strategies to serve diverse user profiles — from advanced traders to speculative and novice traders — adapting the product to their distinct preferences and requirements.
Cross-functional Collaboration
Work closely with Design, Engineering, Data, and Marketing to translate user insights into shipped product features and iterative improvements.
Collaborate with UX/UI designers to optimize trading interface layout and usability, ensuring a seamless and intuitive experience.
Partner with Engineering to ensure efficient feature implementation, maintaining a balance between innovation and operational feasibility.
Measure the impact of product initiatives through well-defined metrics, using data-driven insights to refine strategies and deliver measurable outcomes.
What We Look For In You
5+ years of product management experience with a demonstrated track record in consumer-facing product, ideally in trading, fintech, or crypto.
Solid understanding of manual trading workflows across mobile and web — including the needs and behaviors of different trader personas.
Strong ability to translate user research and local market insights into actionable product roadmaps.
Excellent product sense, attention to detail, and a history of shipping products that users love.
Strong analytical skills — comfortable working with data to prioritize, validate hypotheses, and measure outcomes.
Proven cross-functional leadership — able to align design, engineering, data, and commercial teams around a shared vision.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey complex ideas clearly to diverse stakeholders.
Nice-To-Haves
Proficiency in Spanish and/or Portuguese. Candidates who can engage with LatAm users and stakeholders in local languages will have a strong advantage, though this is not a strict requirement.
Direct experience in the Latin American market — understanding of local user behaviors, payment ecosystems, regulatory environments, and cultural nuances across the region.
Hands-on trading experience in FX, stocks, or crypto.
Familiarity with technical analysis tools and charting platforms.
Experience working in globally distributed teams with cross-regional collaboration.

Ginmon ist einer der führenden digitalen Vermögensverwalter in Deutschland.

Seit der Gründung im Jahr 2014 in Frankfurt am Main verfolgt das Unternehmen die Mission, professionelles, wissenschaftlich fundiertes Vermögensmanagement einer breiten Zielgruppe zugänglich zu machen: transparent, kosteneffizient und vollständig digital. Über die eigene Plattform investieren Kundinnen und Kunden automatisiert in global diversifizierte ETF-Portfolios, die kontinuierlich optimiert und an individuelle Anlageziele angepasst werden.

Mit Ginmon Technology bietet das Unternehmen zusätzlich seine Technologie und Investment Expertise im B2B-Bereich an und ermöglicht es Banken und Finanzdienstleistern, digitale Vermögensverwaltungslösungen unter eigener Marke in ihr Produktangebot zu integrieren.

Du führst Markt- und Nutzerforschung durch und identifizierst neue Produkt-Features und Trends im Bereich WealthTech.

Du entwickelst die Produkt Roadmap und erarbeitest gemeinsam mit funktionsübergreifenden Teams detaillierte Produktanforderungen, User Stories und Abnahmekriterien.
Du arbeitest eng mit verschiedenen Abteilungen im Unternehmen sowie mit externen Partnern und Interessengruppen zusammen und stimmst dich regelmäßig mit ihnen ab.
Du stellst sicher, dass Produktfunktionen spezifikationsgerecht, in hoher Qualität und termingerecht umgesetzt werden.
Du beobachtest die Leistung bestehender Funktionen und der zugrunde liegenden Plattform und identifizierst Potenziale für technische Optimierungen und UX-Verbesserungen.
Du übernimmst vollständige Verantwortung für deine eigenen Themenbereiche und trägst aktiv zu Produktentscheidungen bei.
Dein Profil
Du hast ein erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Studium.
Du bringst mindestens 3 bis 5 Jahre praktische Erfahrung im Produktmanagement oder Software-Engineering mit, idealerweise im Fintech- oder Start-up-Umfeld.
Du kennst dich sehr gut mit agilen Methoden wie Scrum sowie dem gesamten Software-Entwicklungszyklus aus.
Du hast einen sicheren Umgang mit Tools wie Jira, Claude for Design, Framer, Grafana, Brevo oder Figma.
Du arbeitest sowohl selbstständig als auch im Team und triffst eigenständig fundierte Entscheidungen.
Du kommunizierst sicher und transparent innerhalb deines Teams, unternehmensweit (auch mit CTO und CEO) sowie mit externen Stakeholdern.
Du sprichst fließend Englisch und Deutsch (mindestens C1).
Du lebst im Rhein-Main-Gebiet und kannst mindestens 60 % deiner Arbeitszeit in unserem Büro in Frankfurt am Main verbringen.
Warum Ginmon?
Hohes Maß an Autonomie und die Möglichkeit, unsere Produktstrategie in enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem Management-Team aktiv mitzugestalten.
Ein dynamisches, internationales Team mit flachen Hierarchien, schnellen Entscheidungswegen und einer "Get-things-done"-Mentalität.
Wettbewerbsfähiges Gehalt mit einem attraktiven, erfolgsorientierten Bonussystem, gekoppelt an deine Partnership-Meilensteine.
Beteiligung am langfristigen Erfolg von Ginmon durch ein Virtual Employee Share Option Program (VESOP).
Spezielle Konditionen für Mitarbeiterinvestments und Nutzung unserer Plattform;
Hybrides Arbeiten (60 % vor Ort) und flexible Arbeitszeiten.
Modernes Büro im Herzen Frankfurts mit High-End-Equipment und optimaler ÖPNV-Anbindung.
Regelmäßige Teamevents und eine angenehme Büroatmosphäre (Snacks, Getränke, Firmen-Merch u. v. m.).
Erstattung deiner Internetkosten und der Kosten für dein Deutschlandticket.
Vielfältige Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten.

Define and execute the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for BAD Product systems.
Uncover user friction through customer research, support data, telemetry, and feedback from internal teams.
Map and improve end-to-end customer journeys covering purchasing, subscriptions, licensing, and administration.
Identify gaps, overlaps, and inconsistencies across sub-systems to build a clear, unified user experience.
Partner with engineering, design, analytics, and QA from early discovery through launch and continuous iteration.
Define and track key product metrics for adoption, conversion, and support demand.
Communicate product direction, trade-offs, and progress clearly to cross-functional stakeholders.

An ownership mindset, taking responsibility for outcomes, not just task completion.
A clear focus on underlying problems and desired outcomes rather than immediate feature requests.
Comfort with technical complexity, trade-offs, and systems thinking.
A preference for quality, long-term sustainability, and user trust over short-term fixes.
The ability to make grounded decisions using customer research, analytics, and experimentation.
Strong collaboration skills across multi-disciplinary teams and distinct business areas.

A proven track record of managing technically complex SaaS, enterprise, or B2B product areas end to end.
Hands-on experience driving product discovery, user research, and roadmap prioritization.
Experience navigating complex customer journeys, multi-team dependencies, and cross-functional stakeholders.
Experience making data-informed decisions using telemetry, product metrics, and experimentation.
The ability to work comfortably alongside engineering teams on technical details, APIs, data models, and system integrations.
Fluency in English.
What success looks like
In practice, success means building a licensing and administration experience that feels seamless to the user and resilient under the hood. You'll bring clarity to ambiguous systems, simplify fragmented customer flows, and establish reliable product metrics. Distribusion is the world’s leading ground transportation marketplace and gives travelers seamless access to ground transportation online, from search to ticket purchase. We have built a cutting-edge B2B technology platform that connects bus, rail, and ferry operators in 70+ countries with the biggest online retailers, including Google Maps and Booking.com.
We are shaping the future of travel and building the largest global network of transport providers and retailers. Having grown 10x in the past year, we are one of the fastest-growing startups in travel. Backed by four leading VCs (TQ Ventures, Creandum, Northzone, and Lightrock), and now, following our recent $80 m Series C, we are ready to push beyond.
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to build the payment infrastructure behind millions of transactions.
Distribusion is transforming from a marketplace enabler to a global travel infrastructure provider — and Financial Services is our newest, highest-impact department. You'll define the systems that sit between our customers, our merchants, and the global payments ecosystem — building for reliability, conversion, and scale.

Own the product vision and roadmap for payments, checkout, fraud, and routing

Define KPIs and frameworks for PSP performance, fraud rates, and acceptance

You’ll turn payments into a growth driver — boosting acceptance, reducing fraud, and improving conversion

Drive real business impact through higher acceptance rates, lower fraud, and improved conversion

s.h: About the role: What's in the Box
s.t:
As the Senior Product Manager II for Menu Planning within the Operations Mega Alliance, you will own the product layer that decides what lands on HelloFresh menus every week, across markets, brands, and millions of customers.

You will drive the systems and workflows that let our culinary, commercial, and operations teams plan, version, and scale an ever-expanding menu, working back from their needs to build the automation and data foundations that make a larger and more personalized assortment possible.
This is a domain in the middle of a significant platform transformation: you will help move menu planning into a smarter baseline, all while keeping weekly menu delivery running without disruption. You will partner closely with engineering, culinary, procurement, and stakeholders across our largest markets to define a data-driven roadmap, untangle real complexity around regionality and menu customization, and set the long-term vision for how HelloFresh builds its menu at scale.

Own the vision and multi-quarter roadmap for menu planning, turning the needs of culinary, commercial, and operations partners into prioritized initiatives tied to clear business impact.
Build scalable systems and data foundations for menu versioning, regionality, and customization that make a larger, more personalized assortment possible.
Leverage AI and machine learning to automate menu and editorial workflows and sharpen assortment decisions, partnering with data science to take models from concept to production.
Collaborate with engineers, data scientists, and senior stakeholders across our largest markets to gather requirements, align in direction, and secure buy-in for strategic bets.
Apply a data-driven approach, using both qualitative and quantitative signals to validate hypotheses, prioritize, and measure outcomes.
Champion product craft as the hands-on expert for menu planning, raising the bar on discovery, prioritization, and execution across the tribe.

Seasoned product experience building and scaling technical or platform products, ideally in a domain with real operational or supply-chain complexity.
Ability to navigate ambiguity , shaping strategy in undefined problem spaces without waiting for a predefined solution.
Data-driven decision-making , comfortable using both qualitative and quantitative signals to validate hypotheses, prioritize, and prove impact.
Fluency working alongside engineers, designers and data people , enough to understand technical trade-offs, feasibility, and how AI and machine learning can be applied to real workflows.
Strong communication and stakeholder skills , with a knack for aligning and influencing partners at every level and steering cross-functional teams toward shared goals.
Proven knack for structure , breaking multifaceted problems into parts others can act on.

You’ll receive a competitive salary package, including a HelloFresh-subsidized pension scheme.
Enjoy savings on your weekly HelloFresh box.
Support your mental wellbeing with access to platforms like Headspace and Spill.
Stay active with 24/7 office gym access, a discounted Urban Sports Club membership, and other wellbeing resources.
Balance your life with our flexible hybrid model.
Recharge with sabbatical leave options in addition to standard time off.
Embrace "Learning Never Stops" with internal training, the HelloFresh Academy, and a dedicated budget for German language courses.
Enjoy tasty in-office meal deals and fresh food options.
We support working families with parent-friendly policies, an in-office kids corner, and an on-site babysitter.

We're building a new global Berlitz, and this is your opportunity to help shape it. Nearly 150 years of expertise, meeting the ambition and technology to power a new era of learning.
If you are the kind of person who thrives in a fast-paced environment, isn’t afraid of a blank page, and is excited to help shape the future of a global company undergoing a significant transformation, you might belong at Berlitz!
We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the experience our customers live in every day. Right now, using our product means juggling different tools for leads, performance tracking, billing, compliance, and support.
This isn't a maintenance role. It's a build from the ground up mandate for a product that will touch every customer we have, in every market we operate.

Own the customer experience end to end, from lead and pipeline management to performance tracking, billing transparency, compliance, and support, unified into one clear, trustworthy product.
Design for a genuinely multi sided user base. Customers, their internal teams, and our own internal teams all need different views of the same truth. You'll figure out how to serve all of them without compromise.
Turn customer pain into product decisions. Talk directly to customers across our markets, translate what you hear into a sharp, prioritized roadmap, and ship things that make their day to day genuinely easier.
Drive company wide visibility and growth. Give both customers and internal teams a real time, trustworthy picture of how the business is performing, market by market.
Use AI as your default tool, not a side project. Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, and modern AI prototyping tools are part of your daily workflow for discovery, prototyping, PRD creation, and execution.
Move fast, end to end. Take ideas from research and discovery through validation, launch, and iteration, using AI assisted workflows to compress the cycle from "we think" to "we know."
Champion the initiative internally. Build the case, rally the stakeholders, and be the person who makes this initiative impossible to ignore.

5+ years in product management, ideally with exposure to B2B partner ecosystems or enterprise SaaS.
You're energized by complexity, not intimidated by it. Multiple user types, multiple markets, multiple stakeholders, one coherent product.
You build influence through clarity and trust, not title. You can walk out of a customer conversation and straight into a prioritized roadmap, without losing the thread.
Sharp analytical instincts paired with a genuine builder mindset. You'd rather ship a prototype than write another slide.
A collaborative operator who makes the people around them better.
Why You Should Join
You'll be the product owner for something customers around the world will use every single day, with the freedom to shape it from the ground up, backed by modern AI tooling and a company that's serious about giving its customers a genuinely great product, not just a good enough one.
At Berlitz, connecting people across languages and cultures is at the heart of what we do. Our global workplace reflects the diverse world we serve, bringing together different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. We create an inclusive environment where everyone has an equal opportunity to belong, contribute and grow.
Ready to shape what’s next? Join us and help build the future with us.

Before anything reaches development, ideas must be well thought through from both business and technical perspectives, with particular attention to reliability, compliance, and security.

Rockstar is recruiting for a company that builds the connective tissue for defense acquisition. Their platform lets engineering models, simulations, and digital threads move securely across primes, suppliers, and government program offices, so a system can be tested, trusted, and fielded in months rather than years.

They work at the center of some of the hardest problems in defense acquisition: getting the right model, to the right person, at the right classification, at the right time. They are a small, senior team, and every hire changes what the company can do next.

The company is a platform for sharing and working on engineering data in highly regulated, no-fail industries, where a mistake can cost a mission, an aircraft, or a life.

No single team builds a fighter: the airframe comes from a prime, the engine from one supplier, the radar from another, and the teams are separated by geography, classification level, corporate boundaries, and an ecosystem of software tools.

The company keeps their models, simulations, and test results connected so they can move fast and not break things.
They are hiring a Senior Product Manager to own a significant piece of that platform end to end. You'll take a set of features that each solve a real problem and turn them into a product that hangs together, one coherent story for the customer, one coherent roadmap for the team.
This is a role for someone ambitious who wants real ownership. You'll get a problem space, direct access to customers, and a strong engineering team. From there, we expect you to figure out what matters: talk to users, find the shape of the problem, decide what to build and in what order, and carry it through to shipped. You'll work directly with their Head of Product on strategy. Your job is to bring a clear point of view to that conversation, not to wait for one.
The domain is technical and they like it that way. Their users are systems engineers building spacecraft, hypersonic vehicles, and submarines.

A single customer problem might span extracting proprietary CAD files into vendor-neutral formats, sharing data across air-gapped environments, and automatically re-checking mission requirements on every revision, which means their product touches engineering tools, SDKs, APIs, workflows, and secure infrastructure.

You don't need to be able to administer a Kubernetes cluster, but a conversation about one shouldn't scare you. You need enough technical depth that engineers trust your judgment and customers trust your answers.
You don't need to have run a business or owned a massive roadmap. You do need to be comfortable in a room with senior stakeholders (a customer's chief engineer, a program executive, their leadership team) and able to hold your own.

Own a product area end to end: define what success means, build and manage the roadmap, and make the calls on what to build next and what not to build at all.
Create coherence: take a collection of features and turn them into a product customers understand and a narrative the company can sell.
Do real customer research: get in front of users, understand their workflows and constraints, and turn what you learn into product decisions.
Work day to day with a senior engineering team: write crisp specs, make fast decisions when they're blocked, and protect their time from everything that isn't the work.
Partner with their Head of Product on strategy: bring the evidence, argue for a direction, and help decide where the product goes next.
Communicate with senior stakeholders: engage credibly with customers, sales, and leadership, and represent your area to all of them.

s.h: Requirements and Who Thrives in This Role
s.t:
They hire for judgment, curiosity, and a bias toward action more than for a specific degree or years of experience. That said, people who do well in this role tend to share a few things:
4+ years of product management experience at a company known for shipping excellent product at speed, think Stripe, Ramp, Datadog, or an equivalent high-caliber environment.
A track record of shipping under ambiguity: you've taken complicated, ambiguous features from idea to shipped with minimal direction, and you've been handed a hard problem and come back with a good answer.
Comfort in technical domains: you've built products for technical users, or products with real infrastructure underneath them, and you can go deep enough to earn an engineer's trust.
Strong customer instincts: you'd rather talk to five users than read fifty tickets, and you know how to turn research into decisions.
Directness: when asked for your best guess, you give it. You don't hedge, and you'd rather say "we're doing this wrong, here's what I'd do instead" than make people guess what you think.
Speed and ownership: you take responsibility for outcomes, not activity, and you move fast enough that the team never waits on you.

Experience as the PM for a CLI-based tool, SDK, or other developer-facing product.
Experience as the PM for a desktop or client application: client software is weird in ways that web/SaaS experience doesn't cover, and they'd benefit from someone who has spent time in those trenches.
Deep technical experience with cloud or security infrastructure, especially on products sold to engineers (B2B tooling for data processing, cloud services, and the like).
Background in aerospace, defense, digital engineering, or other regulated domains.
Must be a US citizen living within the United States.

You will work directly with the executives and engineers building the company, not through layers of process. You will see your work reach real programs and real missions quickly (the products you ship here end up in test events and fielded systems, not slide decks) and you will have room to shape both the product and the product function itself. This is a small team solving a problem that matters, and they are looking for people who want to build the next chapter of it with them.
They've built a team of what they call Wizards: people who bring depth in their domain and range across others, who are collaborative without being deferential, and who genuinely care about what they're building. They celebrate individual contributions, give feedback early and often, and argue about ideas so they can execute together.
There's no room here for hierarchy for its own sake, or for busywork that doesn't move the mission. They are outcomes-driven, and they hold each other to a high standard, with genuine respect for each person's expertise and wellbeing.
Focus is rewarded. Finish is remembered.
Facts are friendly. Even when they are not fun.
Fellowship is fundamental. Make others successful.

About Decagon
Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.
Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.
We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures, along with many others.
We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.

The Product Management team owns Decagon’s platform and foundational features: agent building, eval, analytics, testing, experimentation, versioning, integrations, and enterprise controls. We work across every customer segment, partnering closely with engineering, design, and go-to-market to ensure our platform is robust, scalable, and easy to use.
As one of our founding PMs, you’ll help define the product foundation that every Decagon customer uses to build and run their AI agents. You’ll own initiatives end-to-end, from discovery and scoping to launch and adoption, shaping the product experience for some of the world’s most influential businesses.

Decagon agents take action inside some of the most complex enterprise systems. You'll own everything that makes that possible. Integrations and connections, headless and SDK deployment, external APIs and developer experience, channel expansion and partnerships.
This is the least solved part of enterprise AI. Getting an agent live inside a bank means wiring into systems built decades before LLMs existed, then clearing a security organization whose job is to say no. Everything you productize unlocks the next wave of deployments across our largest customers.

Define the vision, strategy, and roadmap for developer experience, integrations channels, and enterprise readiness
Decide what we build natively, what we make self-serve, and what we open up so customers and partners can extend it themselves
Work with infrastructure and security on data handling, retention, and residency
Drive channel and partner expansion with go-to-market and BD, including marketplace listings and co-sell motions

Higharc is seeking a hands-on Forward Deployed Product Manager to turn a large production homebuilder's unstructured plan catalog into structured, queryable product data. This is a founding role on a brand-new Forward Deployed team.

A homebuilder's plan library is the product data behind its entire business, and at enterprise scale that data is almost entirely unstructured. Plans live as drawing sets scattered across semi-autonomous divisions, renamed and re-numbered as they move. Nobody can say with confidence which plans are duplicates, how many versions of a given home exist, or what actually varies between them.
Higharc converts those catalogs into structured, queryable plan data and builds the analysis on top of it: searchable plan libraries with agent-enabled natural-language search, geometric similarity scoring that surfaces plans which have forked under different names, structured mapping of what varies across a library, and classification that makes consolidation decisions possible.
You'll own what gets built in the field, working embedded alongside our Forward Deployed Engineers and in partnership with the homebuilder to turn plans into actionable data. For years, avatars have been something you watch. You write a script, we render a video, someone presses play. That model has taken AI video a long way but it has a ceiling. A video can't answer a question. It can't read the room. It can't role-play a tough conversation and adapt when you push back.
We're changing that. Interactive Avatars listen, talk, and respond in real time; inside your product, your website, or your internal tools. You bring the logic and the language model; we power the avatar layer: the speech, the expression, the listening, the sense that there's someone actually there.
It's early. Interactive Avatars is in closed beta today, and the teams building on it are pushing it into places we didn't expect - AI sales reps, always-on support agents, interactive trainers, onboarding guides. We're hiring a Product Manager to own it and take it from beta to a platform that thousands of developers build on.
This is a role with real scope. You'll help define what a real-time avatar API should be, the surface developers integrate against, the experience end users feel, and the commercial model that makes it a business. You'll work directly with the engineering and research teams building the real-time avatar stack, and with the design partners already live in the beta.
The problem you're solving
Today, a developer who wants a lifelike, real-time avatar in their product has to stitch together a streaming pipeline, a rendering layer, an agent, and a set of hard real-time problems - latency, interruption handling, listening behavior, expressiveness, consistency across sessions, most of which have nothing to do with the product they're actually trying to build.
We have the avatar technology and a working beta. What we need is a PM who can turn that into an API a developer can integrate in an afternoon, trust in production, and build a real business on top of, all while holding a quality bar high enough that the experience feels human, not uncanny.
What you'll be doing
Owning the end-to-end Interactive Avatar API. This is the developer-facing surface (SDK, integration patterns, docs), the real-time experience quality, and the path from closed beta to general availability, and defining what the roadmap looks like over the coming cycles
Getting close to the developers and teams building on the beta: understanding how they integrate, where the API fights them, which real-time behaviors make or break the experience, and what "production-ready" means to them
Translating that understanding into a clear product direction. What to build, in what order, and why, and keeping the team aligned as the strategy evolves
Working closely with the engineering and research teams building the real-time avatar stack; contributing clear specs, sound judgment on trade-offs (quality vs. latency vs. cost), and the context that helps them build the right thing the first time
Partnering with go-to-market and commercial teams to define how the API is packaged, priced, and sold - a real-time API has a fundamentally different business model from batch video, and shaping that is part of the job
Defining and tracking the metrics that tell us whether the product is working across adoption, integration success, real-time quality, reliability, and the commercial signals that prove it's a business

You've owned a developer-facing product before like an API, an SDK, or a platform and you know that the product is the developer experience. You understand that adoption is won or lost in the first hour of integration, and that trust is won or lost the first time something breaks in production. You build accordingly.
You're comfortable in a space where the roadmap isn't fully formed. You don't need a clean brief to get started. You can talk to developers, watch them integrate, synthesize what you see, and come back with a point of view. You care about the detail, and you can hold a quality bar for something subjective and hard: a real-time avatar either feels present and responsive or it feels off, and the difference lives in latency, interruption handling, expressiveness, and consistency. You know how to make that bar concrete and defend it.
You think commercially. A new API isn't just a technical surface. It's a business, and you have instincts (or scar tissue) around how developer products get adopted, packaged, and monetized.

Join Axon and be a Force for Good.
At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.
Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.
About Axon
Axon’s mission is simple and bold: Protect Life .
We build technology that helps first responders, security teams, and communities act with speed, clarity, and confidence in the moments that matter most. Our Real-Time Operations (RTO) portfolio, anchored by the Fusus platform, is transforming how law enforcement, enterprise security, and international agencies detect, assess, and respond to threats.
Fusus connects live video, alerts, sensors, and location data into a unified operating picture, accessible on any device. Alerts and presence are the heartbeat of that picture. They determine what demands attention and who is in position to act. We're building intelligent, high-signal alerting and presence experiences that cut through noise and keep operators and responders locked into what matters most.

As Senior Product Manager for Alerts & Presence, you will define and lead the roadmap for how Fusus surfaces the right information to the right people at the right time - making alerts and responder presence the connective tissue of real-time operations.
You'll build the systems that determine what warrants attention, how it's prioritized and routed, and how operators maintain awareness of who is where. This spans alert generation from cameras, sensors, LPR, drones, and third-party sources, as well as the presence layer that tracks responder locations, unit status, and asset proximity.
Your work will enable officers, security teams, and emergency responders around the world to cut through noise, act on what matters, and coordinate with confidence. By making alerts smarter and presence data seamless, your work will help prevent harm, accelerate response, and directly advance Axon's mission to Protect Life.
Work Location: This role is based out of our London office and follows a hybrid schedule. We rely on in-person collaboration and ask that team members work onsite Tuesdays through Fridays, with the flexibility to work remotely on Mondays, unless there is an approved workplace accommodation. We believe that connection fuels innovation, and our in-office culture is designed to foster meaningful teamwork, mentorship, and shared success.

Presence data gives commanders and dispatchers clear visibility into who is where - improving coordination and resource deployment
Adoption grows across customer segments with high daily use, strong retention, and positive field feedback
Every second saved contributes to safer outcomes for officers, teams, and the public
